issues: Whether the Indian Act section 87 tax exemption can apply to off-reserve employment income of a status Indian
Whether a motion to strike is the appropriate procedural vehicle to dispose of constitutional and section 35 claims at the pleading stage, and what standard applies
Whether section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 can be invoked to challenge the tax treatment of off-reserve employment income of status Indians
Whether the Crown's duty to consult can be invoked to challenge the application of tax legislation to off-reserve income of status Indians
Whether the Crown's fiduciary duty to Indigenous peoples can ground a challenge to the tax treatment of off-reserve employment income
Whether section 15 of the Charter is engaged by the differential tax treatment of on-reserve versus off-reserve income of status Indians
Whether the Tax Court of Canada has jurisdiction to hear and determine claims based on section 35 Aboriginal rights or inherent Indigenous rights
Whether the absence of Indigenous consent to taxation or the failure to convene a constitutional conference can invalidate the application of tax law to status Indians
key_facts: Both taxpayers are registered status Indians and members of different First Nations
Both lived and worked off-reserve in a large city
Employment was through a placement agency that hired out Indigenous workers to urban social service organizations
One worked part-time as an Indigenous support worker; the other at an Indigenous legal clinic
Tax authority reassessed on the basis that the income was not situated on a reserve and thus outside the Indian Act exemption
Taxpayers filed appeals raising constitutional, inherent-rights, duty-to-consult, and fiduciary-duty arguments
Crown moved to strike the appeals and the constitutional notice
causes_of_action: motion to strike constitutional and s. 35 claims
candidate_statutes: Indian Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. I-5, s. 87
Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.)
